express.definition:
n. mail that is distributed by a rapid and efficient system
n. public transport consisting of a fast train or bus that makes only a few scheduled stops
n. rapid transport of goods
v. give expression to
express.translation:
n. 快车, 快递, 专使
a. 明确的, 丝毫不差的, 专门的, 快的
vt. 表达, 表示, 表露

express a letter to.translation: 用快邮给某人寄一封信,给某人寄一封快信

express agreement.translation: [法] 明示协定, 明示协议

express authority.translation: [法] 明示授权, 明示权限

express declaration.translation: [法] 明示宣言, 明示宣告

express feelings.translation:
抒发情感
表达感受（express feeling的复数）

express oneself.translation: 表达自己的意思;表达自己的感情

express regret over the death of.word: express regret over the death of

express waiver.translation: [法] 明示放弃, 明示弃权书

express warranty.translation:

express-mail.definition: v send by express mail or courier

expressed almond oil.translation: [医] 压制扁桃[仁]油, [甜]扁桃[仁]油

expresser.definition:
s not tacit or implied

expresses.definition:
n mail that is distributed by a rapid and efficient system
n public transport consisting of a fast train or bus that makes only a few scheduled stops
n rapid transport of goods
v give expression to
v articulate; either verbally or with a cry, shout, or noise
v serve as a means for expressing something
v indicate through a symbol, formula, etc.
v manifest the effects of (a gene or genetic trait)
v obtain from a substance, as by mechanical action
v send by rapid transport or special messenger service
expresses.translation: n. 快车( express的名词复数 ); <英>快运; [E-]快报; 快件服务

expressible.translation: a. 可表现的, 可榨出的

expressing.definition: p. pr. & vb. n. of Express

expression.definition:
n. the feelings expressed on a person's face
n. expression without words
n. the communication (in speech or writing) of your beliefs or opinions
n. (genetics) the process of expressing a gene
expression.translation:
n. 表达, 表现, 词语, 措辞
[计] 表达式

expressional.definition:
a. Of, or relating to, expression; phraseological; also,
   vividly representing or suggesting an idea or sentiment.
expressional.translation: a. 表现的, 表情的

expressionism.definition: n. an art movement early in the 20th century; the artist's subjective expression of inner experiences was emphasized; an inner feeling was expressed through a distorted rendition of reality

expressionist.definition:
n. an artist who is an adherent of expressionism
a. of or relating to expressionism
expressionist.translation:
n. 表现派作家
a. 表现主义的

expressionistic.definition: a of or relating to expressionism
expressionistic.translation: a. 表现主义的, 有表现派作风的

expressionists.definition:
plural of expressionist
n. an artist who is an adherent of expressionism
a. of or relating to expressionism
expressionists.translation:
(expressionist 的复数) n. 表现派作家
a. 表现主义的

expressions.definition:
n the feelings expressed on a person's face
n expression without words
n the communication (in speech or writing) of your beliefs or opinions
n a word or phrase that particular people use in particular situations
n the style of expressing yourself
n a group of symbols that make a mathematical statement
n (genetics) the process of expressing a gene
n a group of words that form a constituent of a sentence and are considered as a single unit
n the act of forcing something out by squeezing or pressing
expressions.translation: n. 表情；公式；表达式；表示式（expression是复数形式）

expressure.definition:
